newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians upbeat about the econony in '97 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians upbeat about the econony in '97 - poll.

text.p: A new Gallup-Gazeta Mercantil poll shows Brazilians are very optimistic about the economy's prospects for the next 12 months with 66 percent of those polled saying 1997 will be a better year than 1996.
The poll, published Thursday in financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, showed the highest income groups were the most upbeat with 80 percent of those polled saying 1997 will be better than 1996.

The middle and lower income groups, those which should most benefit from the stabilization of the economy, are more conservative in their predictions. Sixty-two percent of the middle income group forecast a better 1997 while 66 percent of the lower income groups said next year would be better than the last.
The Gallup poll interviewed 1,250 people over the age of 16 between November 14 and December 5.

Gallup said the optimism index -- which is measured as the difference between the percentage of those who are optimistic and the percentage of those who are pessimistic -- was the second highest since the index began to be measured in 1981.

More significant was the fact that the 1996 index (52 points) was only exceeded by the 1994 index (58 points) which was measured immediately after the implementation of the Real anti-inflation plan and on the eve of the swearing-in of the new Cardoso administration.
